This is the Hope Diamond, and legend says it brings bad luck to anyone who owns it.
A French trader bought it in India and sold it to King Louis the Fourteenth, who had it cut into the French Blue.
In seventeen ninety-two, thieves stole the French crown jewels, and the French Blue vanished.
Twenty years later, a smaller blue diamond showed up in London. Scientists proved it was cut from the stolen one.
Later it belonged to a banker named Henry Hope, which is how it got its name.
But the curse was mostly made up. Historians think the jeweler Pierre Cartier spread scary stories to sell it to a rich buyer.
Here's the twist. In nineteen fifty-eight, Harry Winston gave it to the Smithsonian. He sent it by regular mail.
Postage was just two dollars and forty-four cents, and the mailman said he didn't believe in the curse.
Today it still glows red under ultraviolet light, like a hot coal.
